title: Conversion
definition: Conversion is the turning of a sinner from sin to God through repentance and faith in Jesus Christ.
summary: Conversion is the God-given turning of a person from sin to Christ in repentance and faith.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Lord to whom sinners turn for mercy, forgiveness, and new life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Conversion describes the decisive reorientation of a life toward Jesus Christ. It includes repentance from sin and faith in the Savior, not merely a religious label, emotional experience, or moral upgrade. The doctrine helps the Church distinguish true Gospel response from surface-level interest.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people can be near Christian things without being turned to Christ. Conversion confronts false security while offering real hope: sinners can be changed, forgiven, and brought into new life. It protects evangelism from counting decisions without looking for the fruit of repentance and faith.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Examine whether your confidence rests in Christ and whether your life is turned toward Him. When sharing the Gospel, call people to more than agreement—call them to repentance and faith. Thank God that no one is too far away for Him to turn around.
